name: kepano/obsidian-skills — 44.9K Stars; Obsidian CEO Ships the Skills He Used Privately

name: Graphify-Labs/graphify — ~105K Stars; Day 20; Knowledge Graph for Any Codebase; 70x Cost Cut
hook: Turns any codebase — plus docs, SQL schemas, configs, and PDFs — into a queryable knowledge graph using local deterministic AST parsing (tree-sitter, 158 languages). A PreToolUse hook routes every file-search through the graph; 15 MCP tools add path tracing, dead-code detection, and architecture analysis. MindStudio benchmarks show up to 70x cost reduction on 500+ file projects. ~105K stars; twenty straight days as the leading codebase-graph tool in the ecosystem.
install: uv tool install graphifyy && graphify install

hook: A multi-agent pipeline scans your project, extracts every file, function, class, and dependency, then saves a queryable graph to .ua/knowledge-graph.json and opens a React + TypeScript web dashboard with color-coded architectural layers, full-text search, and plain-English node explanations. name: DietrichGebert/ponytail — ~101K Stars; Day 5; Laziness Ladder Cuts Code 54–94%
hook: ~101,000 stars. A Claude Code skill that enforces a 7-rung laziness ladder before writing a single line of custom code: stdlib first, native platform features second, existing dependencies third, one-liners before functions, and so on. Benchmarked at ~54% less code (range up to 94%), ~20% cheaper, and ~27% faster on real FastAPI + React sessions. Unlike caveman, which targets prose verbosity, ponytail targets code bloat while preserving security and accessibility guardrails.

name: JuliusBrussee/caveman — ~97.7K Stars; Day 19; 65% Fewer Output Tokens
hook: Compresses agent responses into terse caveman-speak without losing technical accuracy — code, commands, and error messages remain byte-for-byte exact, only the prose is stripped. 65% average output token reduction (range 22–87% across 1,200 test scenarios). The `/caveman-compress` companion shrinks CLAUDE.md and other memory files by ~46%, saving input tokens on every future session permanently. ~97.7K stars; approaching 100K.
recurring_note: ↑ Day 19 — ~97.7K stars; canonical output-token compression tool

name: thedotmack/claude-mem — ~90.8K Stars; Day 6; Persistent Context Across Sessions
hook: ~90,800 stars. Captures everything Claude does across sessions, compresses with AI, and injects relevant context automatically into new sessions via lifecycle hooks — no manual context management. Three-layer progressive-disclosure architecture (search → timeline → fetch) cuts memory token overhead by ~10x vs naively injecting full history. Works with Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, and Gemini CLI.

name: rtk-ai/rtk — ~76K Stars; Day 2; Rust Token Killer; Up to 90% Bash Output Compression
hook: RTK is a CLI proxy that intercepts and compresses shell command outputs before they reach your LLM agent — cutting up to 90% of the bash output Claude reads from git, cargo, pytest, docker, kubectl, AWS CLI, and 96 other commands. An auto-rewrite hook transparently converts commands to their RTK equivalents with zero workflow changes; works with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and 12 other AI tools. Single zero-dependency Rust binary; ~76K stars.

name: multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills — ~195K Stars; Day 25; 4 Rules That Stop Claude Breaking Code

Drop-in for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and 60+ other agents.

MIT license.

name: Claude Code Self-Hosted Environments — Day 2; Run Sessions on Your Own Infrastructure
hook: Shipped in v2.1.224 on August 7, 2026: `claude self-hosted-runner` turns any machine or container into the compute layer where Claude Code web, mobile, and desktop sessions execute — running inside your own network, next to internal services, toolchains, and compliance controls. Repository checkouts, build artifacts, secrets, and any files a session creates stay on your infrastructure. Available on Team and Enterprise plans; supports fixed or on-demand runners.

name: Claude Code Cross-Session Messaging — New; Sessions Can Now Talk to Each Other
hook: Shipped in v2.1.224 (August 7, 2026): two new tools — `ListAgents` discovers other active Claude Code sessions on the same machine, `SendMessage` delivers text to them mid-task. Only text passes (no history, files, or permissions). Use cases: one session warns another when a shared dependency changes, an orchestrator hands a subtask summary to a specialist agent, or two parallel agents coordinate without manual copy-paste. Available on macOS and Linux (including WSL 2); not native Windows. Extended in v2.1.225: SendMessage can now reach Remote Control sessions on other machines by name. Covered by MacRumors, 9to5Mac, MLQ News, and Medium.
